sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under Section 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for grant of compensation.
2. Respondent No. 1 is the insurer, Respondent No. 2 is the owner and Respondent No. 3 is the driver of the offending vehicle.

3. It is stated in this claim petition that on 24.06.2006, the claimant was travelling with his colleagues in the Bus bearing Registration No. AS12/3611 under Assam State Road Transport Corporation but the bus turned turtle and the leg of the claimant was trapped resulting in Right Leg below Knee Amputation, Open Fracture Right Femur, Open Left Metatarsal Laceration Foot and Permanent Disability.
4. Claimant has stated that FIR No. 199/06 was registered under Section 279/337 and 338 of IPC at Police Station Dalgaon, Assam.
5. Claimant has stated that he remained hospitalized for about seven months and incurred nearly Rs. 5,50,000/ on his treatment, special diet, post care operation etc.
6. Claimant has stated that at the time of accident, his age was 38 years and he was working as a Sergeant in Indian Air Force at a salary of Rs. 20,000/ per month.
7. Claimant has stated that the accident was caused by Respondent No. 3 while driving the offending vehicle rashly and negligently.

8. Claimant has stated that before this accident, he was physically fit but now after amputation of his leg, he is declared medically unfit and is kept in Medical Category 'C' (A4G4) and earlier his Medical Category was 'A' (A4G1).
9.
Claimant has stated that at least he would have been promoted upto the rank of Master Warrant Officer.
However, due to accidental injuries, his promotional avenues were shuttered down.
He has claimed a compensation of Rs. 32,19,941/ towards difference in the salary drawn by him today and the salary he may have drawn after promotion, if he had not suffered with accidental injuries.

10. Claimant has also stated that he was a Post Graduate with first division in English literature having a great chances to become a Commissioned Officer in the Indian Air Force and may have reached upto the rank of Group Captain in the normal procedure adopted for promotions.

11. Claimant has stated that he was pursuing MBA from IGNOU and the validity of entrance test was upto September, 2006 but during that period he was hospitalized due to accidental injuries.
12.

Claimant has further stated that the studies of his two daughters were disrupted due to this accident and in case, he is discharged from his service due to this accident, it will be extremely Shri Raja Ram Yadav vs The New India Assurance Co. 30. On the basis of pleadings of parties, evidence on record, issuewise findings are as under:
ISSUE NO. 1: 
31.
Burden of proving this issue is on the claimant.

32. For succeeding in a claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, it is for the claimant to prove that the vehicle which caused the accident was being driven rashly and negligently by its driver.
33. This is sine qua non for getting the relief.

34. The claimant has stated that on 24.06.2006, he along with other Air Force personnel was travelling in the bus bearing No. AS12/3611 under ASTC which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner and without caring for the safety of others by its driver.
35. Respondent No. 3 was the best person to deny allegations of rash and negligent driving made against him in the claim petition but for the reasons best known to him, he was proceeded ex parte.
Therefore, allegations of negligent driving made by the claimant against Respondent No. 3 remained unchallenged.

36. Moreover, when the claimant entered in the witness box and reiterated allegations of rash and negligent driving against Respondent No. 3, again, neither Respondent No. 3 cross examined the claimant nor entered in the witness box to prove his innocence.

37. Photographs of the bus shows that it had fallen on one side of the road which could not have been for any other reason except negligent driving by Respondent No. 3.
38.

Police after investigation in the matter has filed charge sheet against Respondent No. 1 under Section 279/337/338 of IPC which is also prima facie suggestive of negligence of Respondent No. 3.
39.

In Ranu Bala Paul & Ors. v. Bani Chakraborty & Ors. 1999 ACJ 634, the Hon'ble Gawhati High Court has observed as under: "In deciding a matter tribunal should bear in mind the caution struck by the Apex Court that a claim before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal is neither a criminal case nor a civil case.

sentences.text: Para 15 of the report is extracted hereunder: "15.
In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in F.I.R No. 955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle; (ii)
criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of chargesheet under Sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of F.I.R., wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
Proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.
Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down.

There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of the driver."
42.

ISSUE NO. 2:
44.

In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr., MANU/SC/1018/2010, Civil Appeal No.
8981/2010 decided on 18.10.2010, following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims: i. The compensation payable to the claimant who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr., MANU/SC/1018/2010,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner.
ii. Compensation payable in injury cases is payable under two heads.
They are pecuniary damages (special damages) and non pecuniary damages.

Pecuniary damages have three sub heads which are :
(i) expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) (a) Loss of earning ( and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising of loss of earning during the period of treatment and (b) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (iii) Future medical expenses.

Nonpecuniary damages (General Damage) are (iv) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries (v) loss of amenities (and /or loss of prospects of marriage) and (vi) loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
iii.
In routine personal injury cases compensation is awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation is granted under any of the heads (ii) (b), (iii) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospectus of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
45.

The claimant has suffered open comminuted fracture right femur, open fracture 5th metatarsal with extensive laceration over foot, open comminuted fracture tibia and fibula right with extensive soft tissue loss over the leg.
He had undergone amputation of right leg because of uncontrolled septicemia and ARDS.
He had undergone open reduction and fixation by KNail for fracture femur.
He was advised use of artificial limb and physiotherapy of hip, knee and ankle.
He was admitted in the Army Hospital from 24.06.2006 till 12.01.2007 and he was declared fit only for Sedentary Desk Jobs.

46. In the case of DTC v. Suraj Bhan, MAC APP. No. 196/07 dated 29.01.10 where judgment in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. v. Vijay Kumar Mittal (2008) ACJ 1300 was followed, in case of amputation of limb, non pecuniary compensation of Rs. 3 lacs was awarded.

sentences.text: In the case of Vijay Kumar Mittal (supra), the findings of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 17 are as under: "17.

From the afore noted judicial decisions, a trend which emerges is that between the years 1985 and 1990, the courts have been awarding about Rs. 3 lacs under the head 'Non Pecuniary Damages' for amputation of leg resulting in permanent disability of 50% and above."

48. Therefore, this claimant is also awarded a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/ for Pain and Suffering, Rs.
1,00,000/ for Loss of Amenities of Life and Rs. 1,00,000/ for Loss Due to Disfigurement.
49. Since the claimant is provided with an artificial limb i.e. prosthesis device by Army Hospital, no compensation is awarded in favour of the claimant for artificial leg.
50. There is no evidence of cost of treatment or for purchase of medicines.
It appears that the claimant has received the treatment as well as medicines free of cost from Army Hospital.

Therefore,
no compensation is given to the claimant for cost of treatment or for purchase of medicines.
51. However, the claimant is awarded a compensation of Rs. 15,000/ for Conveyance Charges and he is also awarded a compensation of Rs. 15,000/ for Special Diet.
52. Even if the claimant was given salary during leave period, even then he is to be given compensation for loss of leave due to accidental injuries.
53. The claimant has himself stated in his claim petition that his salary at the time of accident was Rs. 20,000/ per month.
54. Therefore, he is awarded a compensation of Rs. 1,40,000/ for Loss of Leave for a period of seven months.
55. It is well settled that a victim of road traffic accident has to be compensated in terms of money even if gratuitous services are rendered by his family members.
56. In Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. v. Lalita: AIR 1981 Delhi 558, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that there cannot be any deduction if domestic help is obtained from a family member.

entities.text: Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. v. Lalita: AIR 1981 Delhi 558
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court had observed as under:  "........... A wrong doer cannot take advantage of this 'domestic element'.
If the mother renders service to her, instead of a nurse, it is right and just that she should recover compensation for the value of the services that the mother has rendered to her.
Mother's services were necessitated by the wrong doing and the injured should be compensated for it.
(Cunnigharn v. Harrison 3 All E.R. 463)
The services of a wife and mother are worth more than those of a housekeeper because she is in constant attendance and does many more things than a housekeeper.
(Regan v. Williamson (1976) 2 All E.R. 241)."
57. This judgment was again quoted with approval by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Narayan Bahadur v. Sumeet Gupta and Anr., MAC APP. No. 762/11 dated 04.07.12.

His fitness condition is now reduced.

63. Since he has suffered 40% disability and he was a Sergeant in Indian Air Force which needs full fitness, financial loss for the claimant will be at least 20% of the assumed income i.e. Rs. 6,000/
per month or Rs. 72,000/ per annum.
64.
Since claimant was 38 years of age at the time of accident, applying multiplier of 15, loss of future prospects a sum of Rs. 10,80,000/ is awarded towards loss of future prospects.

65. Resultantly, total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs. 15,72,897/ which will be paid with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of this claim petition which is 17.04.2010 till its realization.
66. Next question is which of the respondents is liable to pay this compensation to the claimant?

67. The defence of Insurance Company is that its counsel had sent a notice to the driver and owner of the offending vehicle to produce driving license of the driver, fitness and permit of the vehicle on the date of accident.

The argument of counsel for Insurance Company is that as in spite of service of notice, the required documents were not given to it by the driver and owner of the vehicle, it shows that neither the driver had a driving license nor vehicle had a permit and fitness certificate on the date of accident.
68. Counsel for the Insurance Company also relied on report of its surveyor who in spite of efforts could not verify the driving license, permit and fitness certificate.
Therefore, the Insurance Company prayed for exoneration.
69. Respondent No. 2 and 3 are ex parte.

sentences.text: Perusal of record shows that the claimant has filed on record certified copy of Form54 which is Ex. PW1/I.

As per this, driver of the offending vehicle was having a driving license bearing No.
17274/S/Professional valid upto 01.06.2007.
This driving license is issued by RTO, Tejpur, Assam.

Insurance Company has not examined any witness from RTO, Tejpur, Assam to prove that the driving license was not valid or was a fake driving license.
71.

Merely by sending a notice to produce original driving license of the driver, the Insurance Company is not absolved of its responsibility to prove breach of terms and conditions of policy by the insured.

When a copy of driving license of the driver of offending vehicle was available on record, it was for the insurance company to summon an appropriate witness from the relevant Licensing Authority to show that the driving license was fake.

For this, reliance can be placed on the judgment passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Bajaj Allianze General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Bhikhari Yadav in MAC APP. No. 727/11 dated 03.01.12 as well as the New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Geeta & Ors.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianze General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Bhikhari Yadav in MAC APP. No. 727/11
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Geeta & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: MAC APP. No. 553/07 dated 23.12.11.

In the case of Bhikhari Yadav (Supra), the Hon'ble High Court had held that 'It is settled that in order to avoid the liability,
the onus is on the insurance company to prove that there is breach of the policy conditions by the insured.

The breach committed by the insured must be willful, e.g. where the insured entrusts a vehicle to a duly licensed driver and it is unlawfully driven by any other person not holding a valid and effective driving license, it cannot be said that the owner is guilty of willful breach.

Similarly,
where a vehicle is stolen by a thief holding no license and meets with an accident, it cannot be said that the insured is guilty of a willful breach.
Rather, the insured himself is a victim'.

Further, dealing with permit the Hon'ble High Court held that 'Turning to the second limb of argument i.e. issuance of permit to ply vehicle no. DL1G2715 on the date of the accident, the appellant insurance company did not summon any record from the relevant office of the Delhi Transport Authority that on the date of the accident, the vehicle did not have any permit to ply on the road.

Here again, the insurance company failed to discharge the onus that there was breach of the condition of policy in this regard'.
72.
This Form54 reveals that the vehicle had a route permit issued by the State Transport Authority valid till 24.01.2009.
Therefore, the Insurance Company has not shown that the vehicle was being plied on the road without a valid permit.
73. No witness was examined from the State Transport Authority to show that the offending vehicle was being plied without a valid permit.
Therefore, the Insurance Company has not proved that insured had committed any breach of terms and conditions of policy.
